app-setting.tex.location: prop:setting:align (b) and (c), and the proof of (b): "By \cref{lem:setting:preservation}, $\rho_d(\mathrm{par}(T))\subseteq\mathrm{par}(d)$"
app-setting.tex.problem: (b) and the last clause of (c) are false for C=DT°_F and for C=DT°. The minimality clause of (c) is also false for DT°. The proof step is invalid: the preservation lemma covers only skeleton positions. A parameter that occurs only in an argument of a non-pattern occurrence disappears from every datum whose value does not use that hole, so G need not be a subset of par(r). Counterexamples, computed with dtrc (scratch/align_cex.py and align_cex2.py): (1) DT°_F. Take D={0=0∧(∀x 0=0 ∧ 0=0), 0=0∧(∀x x=x ∧ w0=w0), w0=w0∧(∀x x=0 ∧ w1=0)}. Then T=Q∧(∀xP(x)∧P(c)) covers D, there is a single alignment, Min^al(D)={f0=f0∧(∀xP0(x)∧f1=f2)}, and T is not ⪰~ that member. The same happens with T*=(Q∨¬Q)∧(∀xP(x)→P(c)), all of whose instances are valid; this also breaks experiments prop:exp:oracle(b). (2) DT°. Take D'={∀x(0=0)∧0=0, ∀x(x=x)∧w0=w0, ∀x(x=0)∧w0=0}. Then Min^al(D')={∀x(f0(x)=f1(x))∧f2=f1(u)}. This member is strictly above T=∀x(g(x)=h(x))∧g(c)=h(c), which covers D', and T is above no member. The same gap is in the record's proof of experiments Prop E1-al.
app-setting.tex.fix: Replace (b) and (c) by: "(b) Every $T\in\mathcal C$ that covers $D$ up to renaming and all of whose parameters occur in $\mathrm{skel}(T)$ satisfies $T\gen^{\sim}M$ for some member $M$. (c) $\Min^{\mathrm{al}}_{\mathcal C}(D)$ is finite; no template as in (b) lies strictly below a member; and if $D\subseteq\inst^{\sim}(T^*)$ with $T^*\in\mathcal C$ and every parameter of $T^*$ in $\mathrm{skel}(T^*)$ (in particular if $T^*$ is parameter-free), some member $M$ satisfies $T^*\gen^{\sim}M$." In the proof of (b), write "Every parameter of $T$ lies in $\mathrm{skel}(T)$, so by \cref{lem:setting:preservation} $\rho_d(\mathrm{par}(T))\subseteq\mathrm{par}(d)$." In the proof of (c), write "If some $T$ as in (b) satisfied ...". Add a remark giving counterexample (1) and saying that a parameter occurring only inside an argument of a non-pattern occurrence need not occur in the reference datum. Note that the record's E1-al carries the same restriction, and that experiments.tex:44 and prop:exp:oracle(b) inherit it. Alternative: define alignments as partial injective identifications across all data, not anchored at r. This makes (b) true in general but needs a code change.

With the closedness guard, nocap is therefore never needed in addition. (b) The condition is wrong. By prop:univ:capture(b), Cap(φ) can be empty although a free x_i lies under a binder: in (dB), or in (N) with sentences as data, e.g. φ=(x=0∧∀y(x=y)). In that case no capture guard is needed. In (N) and (dB), even without parameters, it must also exclude capture instances whenever $\Cap(\varphi)\neq\emptyset$ (\cref{prop:univ:capture}(b)), by $\mathrm{nocap}$ or by $\mathrm{closed}$, which implies it; under the $\lambda$ convention this is automatic."

zfc.tex.location: prop:zf:false, parenthetical "For $\ReplS$ in the named encoding with textbook names there is no such pair; see \Cref{prop:zf:coll}."
zfc.tex.problem: prop:zf:coll (record C3) covers only anchor data with (R) and N_y. The non-anchor pair ReplS(x∈y), ReplS(y∈A), whose bodies both have root ∈, has the named lgg ∀A(∀x(x∈A→∃y(V0∈V1∧∀u(V2∈V3→u=y)))→∃Y∀x(x∈A→∃y(y∈Y∧V0∈V1))). Its metavariables are term metavariables only, so the record's guard family (freshness on formula metavariables) learns nothing. Its instance V0:=Y, V1:=y, V2:=V3:=u is false: at A={∅}, Y=∅ the antecedent holds, and the consequent needs y∈Y'∈y, contradicting Foundation. It is ZF-refutable. Script univzf_repls_pair.py confirms it is an lgg instance. The claim holds only if freshness guards are also learned for term metavariables, and the paper neither states nor proves this.
zfc.tex.fix: Replace the parenthetical with: "(The complete list is in \Cref{app:zf:fofail}. For $\ReplS$ in the named encoding with textbook names, anchor data give no such instance: the lgg is truth-sound, \Cref{prop:zf:coll}.)" Optionally add to app:zf:fofail: "Non-anchor pairs can still give false instances when freshness guards are available only for formula metavariables: from $\ReplS(x\in y)$ and $\ReplS(y\in A)$ the lgg has $V_0\in V_1$ at occurrences 1 and 3, and $V_0:=Y$, $V_1:=y$ gives $y\in Y\wedge Y\in y$ in the consequent."
